paper.title: In Prospect and Retrospect: Reflective Memory Management for Long-term Personalized Dialogue Agents
paper.central_claim: Reflective Memory Management (RMM): Prospective Reflection (topic-based summarization into a memory bank with LLM add/merge) plus Retrospective Reflection (online REINFORCE update of a lightweight reranker from LLM citation rewards) improves long-term personalized dialogue, e.g. >5% over the strongest baseline on MSC and LongMemEval.

gap.author_gap: Rigid memory granularity fragments semantic structure; fixed retrievers cannot adapt to domains/users; labeled data for personalized retrievers is expensive.
gap.checked_gap: Both limits are concretely tested: granularity comparison shows fixed units underperform an adaptive-granularity oracle (E009), and direct retriever RL fails without a reranker (E005); but neighbors beyond MemoryBank/LD-Agent are only cited.
lineage: MemoryBank (forgetting-curve memory) / LD-Agent (long/short banks, keyword retrieval) / Theanine (timeline retrieval) -> RMM (topic memory + citation-driven reranker)
gap.closest_adjacent: MemoryBank and LD-Agent (run as baselines per the paper); Theanine, MemGPT, Mem0, A-Mem are named in Related Work but not compared; original texts not in pinned input package
gap.residue: Fragmented topics across turns/sessions; retriever mismatch with how the generator uses evidence.
gap.stakes: RAG Acc 58.8 vs RMM 61.2 (Contriever); Recall@5 54.3 vs 60.4.
gap.method_response: Topic-level summarization with merge; online reranker adapting to generator citations.
gap.remaining_gap: Scaling of memory (no forgetting/pruning), multi-modal, cost, privacy; no comparison with newer memory managers.
unresolved: Whether gains persist against budget-matched memory managers
Whether reranker is updated on test queries

G.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. Two concrete bottlenecks (fixed granularity, fixed retriever) with MemoryBank/LD-Agent re-implemented as baselines and own analyses that probe both (granularity oracle, direct retriever RL collapse); newer memory managers only cited.

M.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. Topic memory and citation-reward reranking are each argued and give distinguishing predictions (reranker needed vs direct retriever RL; PR vs fixed granularity); citation ≠ usefulness is the weak assumption.

X.reason: Opus sides with sol. The in-scope retained object (PR memory bank) is fully reconstructable: extraction and merge prompts (App. D), top-K neighbour retrieval, explicit add/merge decision that handles updated facts; REINFORCE hyper-parameters given. Not 4: no external gate, deletion or rollback, reranker architecture inconsistent (opus:O01), RR update schedule unstated (opus:O03). son55's schedule point concerns the weight module and is charged under E.holdout.

E.measurement.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. LongMemEval Recall@5 against annotated evidence and judge accuracy; MSC METEOR/BERT plus LLM-judge with human agreement κ 0.69–0.71 (inter-human 0.82) on 100 items; citation validity checked only against another Gemini model.

E.causality.reason: Opus sides with sol. +PR/+RR/direct-retriever-RL/full ablations on two datasets are useful, but the obvious alternatives for each load-bearing claim are untested: no random- or no-reward reranker (is the gain the citation reward or the extra K=20 candidate pool?), no budget-matched memory manager for PR's extra extraction/merge calls. Gains with the default retriever are small (Acc +0.8 PR, +1.4 RR). Variance is charged to E.statistics, not here.

E.holdout.reason: Both seats 1; re-checked. PR memory is built only from history sessions, but the headline numbers include RR, whose update/evaluation boundary and reset policy are unstated (opus:O03); single model family; offline-pretraining split exists only for §8.6.

E.statistics.reason: Both seats 1 (A2 ladder): 3-run means, negative ablation (direct retriever RL) and a 100-item human study, but no std/CI; margins of 0.8–2.4 points untested.

E.cost.reason: Opus sides with son55. No calls, tokens, latency or RL-step cost anywhere; the single-call design remark (sol:E012) and the 16×A100 hardware line are not cost evidence, and the Limitations only concede RL 'can be computationally expensive'. Consistent with r01b precedent (qualitative remark ≠ cost report).
